cohort: 333 pregnant women aged 15 to 42 years attending antenatal care at tertiary hospitals in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
finding: The prevalence of urinary incontinence was 24.6% among the pregnant women, and those who delivered by cesarean section had lower odds of UI compared to those who delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: Pregnant women who delivered by cesarean section had lower odds of having urinary incontinence compared to those who delivered vaginally.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy, with data collected from June to July 2016 and symptoms assessed for the preceding month of the interview.
